Play the Band on the MODX

Play the band through a Yamaha MODX over USB: connect, set the timing, compare each site sound against the MODX by ear, and send the winners to the board.

Send the band’s notes to a Yamaha MODX over USB instead of playing the site’s own samples, one instrument at a time. Works in Chrome or Edge (Web MIDI). Nothing changes for anyone without a MODX: until you switch it on here, every page sounds as before.

Connect

Not connected

Plug the MODX in by USB and switch it on first. The browser asks once whether this site may use MIDI. With the box ticked, every Backing Track, lesson and tool that uses the band connects by itself and sends the instruments ticked under Routing to the MODX.

Site only
Box unticked. The site's samples, as before.
Sound module
Box ticked, some instruments routed. Those play on the MODX; the rest stay on the site.
Play along
Sound module, with Local Control on (the board's default): you play the MODX keys over the band.

The Site Band Performance

Make this once on the board and save it in a User slot. Each Part listens on its own channel, so the site can play several instruments at once without touching the board again.

Part Channel Put on it Site instruments
1 1 Electric or upright bass bass, electric bass
2 2 Grand piano or electric piano piano, electric pianos
3 3 Organ with rotary speaker tonewheel organ, church organ
4 4 Guitar every guitar
10 10 Drum kit drums, brushes
11 11 Latin percussion kit congas, bongos

Then, in Utility → Settings → MIDI, check that the MODX receives Bank Select and Program Change, so the button below can call the Performance up. Bank and number: in the Performance list, the User bank is shown with the number of each slot. The defaults below (MSB 63, LSB 32, program 0 = User 1, first slot) are from memory of Yamaha's MIDI tables and not yet checked on the board.

Timing

The computer's speakers and the MODX's are late by different amounts. Press Start: the site plays a stick click and the MODX a rim click at the same time. Move the slider until you hear one click instead of two. Use the speakers or headphones you'll play with.

More than zero holds the MODX back; less than zero sends it earlier (only as far as the site's own delay allows).

Compare

Each row plays the same phrase twice, the site and then the MODX (with the Site Band Performance loaded), so you can pick the better one. Your choices are kept. Route the winners sends every instrument where the MODX won to the board.

Routing

Which instruments go to the MODX, and on which channel. Instruments sharing a channel share a Part.

The pitch-bend range must match the Part's (2 is the usual default) or slides land on the wrong note. The rotary speed CC is what the organ's slow/fast switch sends: 1 (the mod wheel) is a guess, so check which control your organ Performance uses for it.

Drum maps

Which MODX key each drum is on. These start as the General MIDI layout, which Yamaha's standard kits mostly follow. Press ▶ to hear one on the MODX and change the number if it's the wrong drum.

Yamaha MODX
